And also a further reference at T7558 of P432 where he says: "The Black Eagles were the special unit of the Kosovo Liberation Army that was under Ramush's command. At every meeting, the travels to Jasic and later in Prapaqan and in Lluk the arrival at Baran, the oath that the brigade took, this solemn event, on all these occasions Idriz Balaj was present, too, in the capacity of the person responsible for security." And then there is -- I just -- I won't read it, but I'll direct you to it. Paragraph 15 of the statement, exhibited as P344 under seal -- sorry, I think I said P432 I. Meant earlier P342. The T77 -- T -- start again. The T7558 reference is of P342. And then in paragraph 15 of the statement exhibited at P344 under seal, there is some further information which should be taken into account. And also Skender Rexhahmetaj, at paragraph 41 of his 92 ter statement, exhibited as P298, says: "You could see at the meetings that Togeri was close to Ramush Haradinaj. I think they spent time together and that this closeness partly stemmed from that." There is also evidence from Rrustem Tetaj and Shemsedin Cekaj who testified to having met Haradinaj in April 1998 and confirmed that Balaj was with him during those meetings. The underlying evidence for that is cited at paragraph 32 of the brief. Your Honours, also point -- I just picked a few. Point 23. There is a reference in point 23 relating to Mr. Haradinaj appointing soldiers to serve in Jabllanice. I've partly answered this already in -- in the submissions I made earlier relating to the formation of the 2nd Brigade. And P242 is an order which shows that on the 11th of July, Mr. Haradinaj appointed Shemsedin Cekaj to form the 2nd Brigade in the zone which covered Jabllanice. And P248 is an order of the 12th of July issued by Mr. Haradinaj appointing those who would serve under Cekaj in that brigade. Amongst those was Driton Zeneli, who was to sever as the commander of the 2nd Battalion. And Bislim Zyrapi also testified that he visited Jabllanice in mid-July, and indicated at transcript 685 that: "When I visited Jabllanice after the meeting of the General Staff and the Staffs from the operative zones, alongside me when inspecting those units was Sali Veseli, and if I remember correctly at the time, Driton Zeneli as well." And Zyrapi confirmed at T685 that Zeneli reported to Haradinaj. Clearly, he was already operating in Jabllanice on the basis of the orders of the 11th and 12th of July. Your Honours, then just touching the Witness 66 point that Mr. Harvey raised relating to the time and date that Witness 66 refers to, it's right that he did give a date of the 19th of May, but when he was questioned about when the witnesses went -- when the victims disappeared, he was questioned at some length about this. It's at P106, and the transcript references in that exhibit are at 8423 to 8434. And he made it clear under -- having been asked several times about this, he was asked at 8433 -- in fact, just come back just slightly before that. Forgive me a moment. In fact, I'll go back to 8432. "Q. ... on the day that the three men went missing, was there any shelling in the area? "A. About four or five days later in their village. ... "THE INTERPRETER: It's not --" "THE INTERPRETER: There was no --" [sic] -- Question -- "THE INTERPRETER: It's not clear whether the shelling lasted four or was it four days." Judge Orie asked to repeat the question. There was some to'ing and fro'ing between counsel, and then we get to the 8433 as to -- to try to clarify this. So the witness said: "THE WITNESS: [Interpretation] So after they went missing, four or five days later there was nonstop shelling." And Judge Orie said: "JUDGE ORIE: Yes. During all these days or did it start four or five days after they went missing? "THE WITNESS: [Interpretation] Four or five days elapsed before the shelling starting. "JUDGE ORIE: That's clear. And now Ms. Gustafson will you ask more detail where the shelling took place."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do we understand from that? Do we understand, then, that they went missing four or five days after the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: No, before the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But that meant that's -- that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] When the shelling started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That question -- that answers Judge Orie's question --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- to clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Before the shelling started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just -- just read it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just read the question and the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: "JUDGE ORIE: ... During all these days or did it start four or five days after they went missing?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right, after.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: "THE WITNESS: [Interpretation] Four or five days elapsed before the shelling started." I.e., after they went missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. So they -- they went missing four or five days -- now, we know that the shelling started on 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Well, 19, 20, 21st, sometime around there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So they went missing --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- four or five days before then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes. Correct. That's the argument that we've made, and this is -- this is the -- this is the evidence, along with the other evidence of Witness 3 and Witness 80, that supports the timing of the missing of -- of the victims. And it goes on. I won't read it all, but there is more that deals with that issue at 8434. Your Honours, there was a suggestion made at some point by Mr. Harvey relating to -- to prior acquittals, but I'm sure I don't need to say in the context of this retrial it's the evidence in this case upon which Your Honours will make the determinations relating to the counts and not on the basis of anything that may have happened in any other trial on any other occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Except at that we've got to take care of res judicata and "autrefois acquit" and "autrefois convict," shouldn't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I'm, sorry, I didn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We should -- we should --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Res judicata.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. On issues that have not been appealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, for matters that are in issue before you in this case, then res judicata cannot arise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no. Res judicata cannot arise on the counts, but as I understood what Mr. Harvey was saying, he was saying -- he was talking specifically about those issues on which the first trial has given a final judgement and were not appealed, and -- and I understand that the issues before us are things that have been sent back to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the impression I -- he left me with was that things have slipped in which shouldn't have slipped in, and we were going to look with a very fine comb whether there were anything that slipped in that shouldn't have been in, and we would point it out if it is there. If it is not there, of course there's no res judicata, and there's no "autrefois acquit" or "autrefois convict."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: No. I -- that may be relevant for some of the counts for which convictions have already been entered, but in terms of the time-frame of the -- of this indictment and all of the issues that are connected with whether a JCE existed or not, what the accused were or were not doing in relation to the counts, those are live, because those are issues that you have to determine in relation to -- to what -- what was going on, whether there was or wasn't a joint criminal enterprise and the like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. We hear you. We are heard him. When -- we hear both of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, really those are all the submissions that I would wish to make unless there are any things that my colleagues think I should [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Oh, I omitted -- I meant to deal with point 6 also of Mr. Haradinaj's list. If I omitted to do that, can I just deal with that? That's the issue relating to the appointment of Din Krasniqi. And, Your Honours, we again direct you to some further material on this issue. First of all, as Exhibit P347, where Mr. Hasanaj states that: "Ramush Haradinaj came to Vranoq on many occasions. He came to announce the appointment of Din Krasniqi as commander of the Lugu i Baran region, which included about 25 villages, including Vranoq, in mid-April. These representatives have been sent from our village to Glodjan to ask Ramush Haradinaj's approval for this appointment." He then also dealt with that little more in P36, at T8743, when he said he'd only heard that three people had gone to Ramush and didn't know whether they had met him or how it was resolved, but went on to confirm that Din Krasniqi became the commander. "And then, of course, we all supposed that this was done with the approval of Ramush," end quote. Now, consistent with that position -- proposition for Din Krasniqi's appointment comes from Witness 17, who testified in P344, at transcript 7659 to 7660, that Din Krasniqi said that he had been appointed by Ramush. "He told me that on the 12th of July when I arrived Vranoq and when we had the meeting with the commanders of the villages and with Krasniqi." I'm sorry, P342. I misspoke. And there's also further reference at transcript 5741 of P52. Your Honours, the final point that I would make very briefly is in relation to the -- Mr. Harvey made the point about the crossroads. You will recall him saying that if the shelling -- there was fighting going on on the 19th of May, it would be difficult to get from Dollc to Grabanice, which is why if it wasn't going on three or four days earlier, perhaps it was easier to get from Dollc to Grabanice, hence their appearance in the village. It's just a thought. It may be something Your Honours wish to take into account in due course. Your Honours, those, I'm pleased to say, are all of the submissions that I would wish to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rogers. Yes, Mr. -- I did suspect that a rejoinder might come.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. It will be a very, very brief rejoinder just in response to some of the points that Mr. Rogers has raised. The first in relation to the alleged presence in the compound area. Mr. Rogers cited, I think, over a hundred pages of the transcript as authority for that. There is simply no evidence that in relation to the fleeting moment that Witness X, as we referred to him now, whether Witness X says that Mr. Haradinaj was there. There's simply no evidence that that occurred in the compound area or the barracks area. And I refer to the specific transcript pages where he discusses this particular incident, and that's firstly 2382, and then an earlier reference 2349, and then transcript 2420 to 2421 is where he discusses only seeing him very, very briefly. And when those actual transcript pages are looked at, it simply doesn't support allegation that Mr. Rogers is now making.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But hadn't -- hadn't he somewhere else told us where he were -- where they were generally?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes. That's in T2349.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where did he say they were?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: He just said the headquarters generally. He did not specify in any detail that it was the compound or the barracks or any particular area. In relation to the incident with Skender Kuqi, he specifically said that took place in the Staff, and that's at T2374.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But where would the headquarters be?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would refer you to paragraph 93 of our final brief where we list the evidence of other witnesses about the location of the headquarters, and you'll see at 93(D) that Mr. Zyrapi, who testified that he went to Jabllanice in mid-July, said that the KLA command post he believed was situated in Mr. Lahi Brahimaj's house and that that's where the meeting took place and that he was then shown various other positions in -- in the village. Pjeter Shala, and this is at 93(A), said that it was about a five to seven minute walk from Mr. Lahi Brahimaj's house to the barracks building. That was at the entrance of the village, whereas Mr. Brahimaj's house was in the heart of the village, and that was about seven -- five to seven minutes' walk away. And we've then listed the evidence which shows that on each occasion when Mr. Haradinaj, it is said, was in Jabllanice, he wasn't, in fact. There's no evidence, in fact, that he was at the compound area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask a question? The premises that we have been shown through the trial --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- showing the two buildings with a yard and a building that is alleged to have had water, what is that called?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: That's called the compound area or the barracks area. That's at the entrance of the village, and then five to seven minutes away into the heart of the village is where the houses are, and that's where Mr. Zyrapi says that the command post was situated or the Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But -- but --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: -- which is where meetings took place according to the evidence that we've listed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But then any detainee -- okay. On this day, he was -- this person was not a detainee.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: No, and there's no evidence what I'm saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He -- they had been brought from wherever together with the 20 to 30 people. Now, is the position of Mr. Haradinaj's Defence that these people were brought to Lahi Brahimaj's house, which was the headquarters, according to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: No. Our position is that when you look at the evidence that Witness X gives about where this all happened, there was this fleeting moment in late May where he saw Mr. Haradinaj. There's no description in the evidence of where that exactly takes place. And that's why it's wrong for Mr. Rogers to say, "Oh, he's given evidence very clearly that this all took place in the compound and the barracks where detainees were." There's no evidence. That's the fundamental point Mr. Emmerson was making yesterday, that there's no evidence to show that on that occasion, that fleeting moment, that that took place where anyone was detained, and that therefore the Prosecution can't draw any inference that Mr. Haradinaj must have known that there was a detention facility or people were detained there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's the first point. The second, very briefly, is in relation to the list with Skender Kuqi's name on. Mr. Rogers cited to various parts of his 92 ter statement and then evidence in chief. What Mr. Emmerson referred to yesterday was the cross-examination where those particular allegations were scrutinised, and the witness said very clearly - we saw the video of it - very clearly that he didn't know who gave him this list, but he didn't believe that it had anything to do with criminal activities and that he didn't pass this information on to anyone, including Mr. Haradinaj. So it's -- it's in that context that we were trying to show the Trial Chamber that it's so important not just to look at the 92 ter statement, just pick out that one paragraph, or what he might have said in examination-in-chief. It's the whole of the evidence that needs to be looked at, because when that was considered, he made it abundantly clear that he didn't know where this list came from. In fact, as was also pointed out, it was recorded below the appointment of FARK military police officers. The appointment of that unit was the entry above that. So there is an inference that can be made that it might have related to FARK, but, really, the bottom line, in our submission, was that that was the evidence he gave at the end of it, when it was all considered, he couldn't say where that list had come from. And therefore, for the Prosecution to cite his evidence as a firm basis to infer that it's a KLA blacklist that was circulated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To cite his evidence in chief, either in -- by way of an statement or way of evidence in chief in proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Precisely. And that -- that is misleading not to cite his evidence in chief if you're going to rely upon it for a central allegation that this is a list that was circulating that had led to certain people disappearing who -- who are charged on the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: So I just wanted to clarify that was the point we were making yesterday. And exactly the same applies to the list of allegations that were handed up to Your Honours yesterday. Many of them were referred to in Mr. Emmerson's closing speech, some of them not, but the reason why we have submitted this, and it's not comprehensive, it doesn't cover every single allegation, but it's to ensure that if an allegation is made by the Prosecution, that the full evidence, not just the 92 ter or part of the evidence, is brought to Your Honours' attention. In that sense, we hope that it can assess. It doesn't only refer to the evidence of one witness. It may refer to other witnesses to show that really it's important that not only the totality of one witness is looked at but all of the evidence, when put together, does it support the allegation that is made by the Prosecution or not? And that is why we have headed the list -- it's both -- inaccuracies. They are things that are just blatantly wrong. But then also there is evidence that might have been selectively or it has been selectively taken, and it's important that the totality of the evidence is looked at in order that the allegation can be exposed for what it is, that it doesn't support, when the evidence is looked at as a whole, what the Prosecution is alleging. Then the final point that I wanted to -- to mention was in relation, Your Honours, to the order of the 5th of July that -- that Mr. Rogers referred to with Mr. Brahimaj being replaced. We've dealt with this in our brief at paragraph 123, and it's clearly set out there that while we say this order reflects Mr. Haradinaj's authority over appointments to that joint structure that was created on the 23rd of June, it in no way implies close knowledge or de facto day-to-day control over the activities that were continuing in Jabllanice, and certainly it does not imply any knowledge of detention or ill-treatment there. It shows authority over the zonal structure, the appointment of persons within that structure. Mr. Brahimaj was the deputy commander as the evidence shows, but you can't infer from that that therefore he had authority over the specific areas, each and every one of them. The evidence is that he could not command each and every area and did not, in reality, do that. And that's what we were emphasising throughout the submissions yesterday, the horizontal nature in which things continued even after the 23rd of June. So I just wish to emphasise that aspect of our submission again, Your Honour. Your Honours, finally if I can just make one correction for the record. Mr. Harvey said that Mr. Emmerson made an error in referring to what was said in relation to the Skender Kuqi incident. He said this at page 52, line 1, today. In fact, Mr. Emmerson was correct in referring to the evidence of what Witness X said. He made that reference to the evidence at page 2809, line 15, on Monday. That's the correct transcript page, and it does accurately reflect what Witness X did say. So there was no need to correct it. I just wanted to make sure that that was properly cited for -- for the record. Thank you, Your Honour. Those are our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't want to quote what he said on Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: He said: "As to the second occasion," this is Witness X, "says he once saw Mr. Haradinaj remonstrating with Lahi Brahimaj about the ill-treatment of Skender Kuqi." So that was coming from -- from Witness X. I mean, I should add that it was just before that that Mr. Emmerson indicated that the allegations that had been made about Mr. Brahimaj and Mr. Balaj were for other persons to address and that he went on to look at the allegations in relation to Mr. Haradinaj specifically and then he quoted his evidence. And he has actually quoted it correctly is the point I'm just making for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just narrow that range down? I did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]. Just before -- just before you do that, let's just exhaust the entire Defence in terms of --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Certainly. I just wanted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- their rejoinder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: -- to -- I thought maybe now was a good moment. If you would prefer not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: -- I'll do it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. I would prefer it a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have any -- I don't believe you have anything to say Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do. Ever so briefly. Once again, we're back with Witness 66. I think what is painfully evident is that the Chamber needs to read the entirety of this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber will read the entire of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At page 8422 so there is no mistake with regard to what this witness actually testified to: "Q. Witness, when was the last time you saw your cousin, and I'd like to remind you not to mention his name. "A. On the 19th of May, 1998, that was the last time I saw him. "Q. And what was he doing when you last saw him? "A. He was grinding corn, and then he placed it in a sack. He was milling the corn, and then he went on, on to the mill to do that." And his testimony continues from that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Your Honours, on behalf Mr. Brahimaj, we don't have anything further to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Troop. Yes, Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you. Can I just narrow that reference that I gave you for the headquarters point. From 2333 to 2361 will give you -- in fact -- yes, 2361 will give you a fair amount of that, and there is more, in fact, going on from there, 2368. We've -- until 223 -- in fact, 2386. It's dealt with in a number of places, and those are the two main places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rogers. I guess we can adjourn. We shall adjourn to a date to be set for judgement. Court adjourned.
